## My Reasoning

I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father farmed it before me. I know one thing well: wheat in winter, maize in summer. That's what grows here, that's what the cooperative buys, that's what my neighbors grow. I'm not going to change at 73.

My two sons are in Shijiazhuang and Baoding now. It's just me and my wife. My back isn't what it was. I've got 5 mu — I keep it all in crops because sitting land makes no sense to me, but I hire the village machinery cooperative for plowing and the combine at harvest. I can't do that heavy work anymore.

For wheat, I'll do rotary tillage in October before planting — faster than deep ploughing, my body can't manage the labor anyway. I'll use 济麦22, the improved variety from the township seed station. Same fertilizer as always: base fertilizer goes in at planting, urea topdress at green-up. I irrigate before winter sets in, again at green-up, jointing, and grain-fill. Four times. That's what wheat needs here. Spray herbicide in spring, fungicide once at heading.

For maize, I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June — no-tillage saves me time and the soil is fine after 40 years of this rotation. I'll buy Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, same as last three years. Summer rain helps but I'll irrigate at least twice. One herbicide spray after emergence, one pass for corn borer if I see damage.

I expect about 470 jin per mu for wheat, maybe 600 for maize. Not a record year, not a bad year. Steady.
